question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It __has raining__ very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.
solution:
The correct answer is Option 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'It has raining' is grammatically **incorrect.**
 
• The correct form should be 'It is raining' because the present continuous tense describes an action that is currently happening.
 
 
• **Example:** Correct:** It is raining now. **
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *It **is raining**__ very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Shall rain** (वर्षा होगी): This construction is not commonly used in modern English to indicate present action.

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: It **shall rain **now. Correct: It will rain tomorrow.
 
 
 
• **Will be rainy** (बरसाती होगी): This phrase is used for general weather forecast but not for ongoing actions.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: It **will be rainy** now. Correct: Tomorrow will be rainy.
 
 
 
• **Rained** (बरसा): Simple past tense, which does not fit the context of an ongoing action.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: It** rained** now. Correct: It rained yesterday.
